statement: If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.
heath_proof: Let A, BC be two straight lines, and let BC be cut at random at the points D, E; I say that the rectangle contained by A, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by A, BD, that contained by A, DE and that contained by A, EC. For let BF be drawn from B at right angles to BC; [I. 11] let BG be made equal to A, [I. 3] through G let GH be drawn parallel to BC, [I. 31] and through D, E, C let DK, EL, CH be drawn parallel to BG. Then BH is equal to BK, DL, EH. Now BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A; BK is the rectangle A, BD, for it is contained by GB, BD, and BG is equal to A; and DL is the rectangle A, DE, for DK, that is BG [I. 34], is equal to A. Similarly also EH is the rectangle A, EC. Therefore the rectangle A, BC is equal to the rectangle A, BD, the rectangle A, DE and the rectangle A, EC.
ai_proof_text:
2.1
**Statement:** If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.

**Step 1.** Let A and BC be the two straight lines, and let BC be cut at random at the points D and E, so that BC is divided into the segments BD, DE, EC. (Two points of section are taken for definiteness; the argument below is the same for any number of points, one further parallel being drawn for each additional point of section.) It is required to prove that the rectangle contained by A, BC is equal to the rectangles contained by A, BD; by A, DE; and by A, EC together.

**Step 2.** From the point B draw BF at right angles to BC [1.11], so that the angle FBC is right.

**Step 3.** From BF cut off BG equal to A [1.3].

**Step 4.** Through G draw GH parallel to BC [1.31]; and through D, E, C draw DK, EL, CH parallel to BG [1.31], meeting GH at the points K, L, H respectively.

**Step 5.** Since DK, EL, CH are each parallel to BG, they are also parallel to one another [1.30]. Hence each of the figures BK, BL, BH, DL, EH is a parallelogram: its two sides lying along GH and BC are parallel (Step 4), and its two remaining sides are two of the parallels BG, DK, EL, CH.

**Step 6.** A parallelogram having one right angle has all its angles right. For each side of the parallelogram is a straight line falling upon the two parallels that form the adjacent sides, so that the two interior angles on the same side of it together equal two right angles [1.29]; hence each angle adjacent to the right angle is right, and, applying the same reasoning again, so is the angle opposite. Such a parallelogram is rectangular, and is the rectangle contained by the two straight lines about its right angle [D2.1].

**Step 7.** The angle GBC is right (Step 2), and it is an angle of the parallelogram BH; therefore BH is a rectangular parallelogram (Step 6). It is contained by GB, BC, which contain the right angle GBC; and GB is equal to A (Step 3). Therefore BH is the rectangle contained by A, BC [D2.1].

**Step 8.** The angle GBD is the same right angle GBC, and it is an angle of the parallelogram BK; therefore BK is rectangular (Step 6), contained by GB, BD, and GB is equal to A. Therefore BK is the rectangle contained by A, BD [D2.1].

**Step 9.** Since BC falls upon the parallels BG, DK, the exterior angle KDE is equal to the interior and opposite angle GBD [1.29]; but GBD is right, so KDE is right, and DL is a rectangular parallelogram (Step 6) contained by DK, DE. Now in the parallelogram BK the opposite sides BG, DK are equal [1.34]; and BG is equal to A; therefore DK is equal to A [CN1]. Therefore DL is the rectangle contained by A, DE [D2.1].

**Step 10.** In the same way, since BC falls upon the parallels BG, EL, the exterior angle LEC is equal to the interior and opposite angle GBE [1.29], which is right; so EH is a rectangular parallelogram (Step 6) contained by EL, EC. In the parallelogram BL the opposite sides BG, EL are equal [1.34]; and BG is equal to A; therefore EL is equal to A [CN1]. Therefore EH is the rectangle contained by A, EC [D2.1].

**Step 11.** The straight lines DK, EL divide the rectangle BH into the three rectangles BK, DL, EH, and no part of BH lies outside them; therefore BH is equal to BK, DL, EH taken together, the whole being made up of its parts.

**Step 12.** Substituting the descriptions obtained in Steps 7–10: the rectangle contained by A, BC (which is BH) is equal to the rectangle contained by A, BD (which is BK), together with the rectangle contained by A, DE (which is DL) and the rectangle contained by A, EC (which is EH). For any number of points of section the same construction yields one rectangle for each segment, each contained by a straight line equal to A and that segment, and their sum is again the whole rectangle BH.

Therefore, if there be two straight lines and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments. Q.E.D.

Path note: the auxiliary lines DK, EL, CH were drawn as parallels to BG [1.31] rather than as perpendiculars to BC [1.11], since parallels give the parallelogram structure needed for 1.34 directly, and their right angles then follow from 1.29 in one step.
